turns.t: Well, here we are again, and I've got my good cardigan on, so that tells you how seriously I take you. ~
I'm flattered, Doris. And who's this with you? ~
Beverley, Doctor. I'm her carer, I come in every morning and Tuesday and Thursday teatimes. ~
Lovely. So, Doris, it's about six weeks since you broke your hip. How's the walking?
Better than it was, though I'm not winning any races. My daughter says I'm a tortoise with a frame. ~
A tortoise that's getting about, that's the main thing. Any pain when you walk?
It's not so much pain, it's more that my hip is stiff, first thing in the morning especially. It loosens up by the time I've had my toast.
She's quicker after breakfast, that's right. And she's been doing her exercises with the physio sheet every day. ~
That's grand. Any falls since you came home?
Not one. Bev won't let me, she hovers like a hawk.
Not a single fall, Doctor, I'd have rung you.
Good, that's what I wanted to hear. Let's go through the tablets, because I want to be sure they all match what I've got on screen.
I put them out every morning in the little box. There's the amlodipine, 5 mg, once a day, for her blood pressure.
And the one for my bones. I can never remember what it's called.
Alendronic acid, 70 mg once a week. It's Sundays, because she has to take it on an empty stomach and sit up for half an hour.
Perfect, Sundays is a good routine. Anything for pain?
Only the paracetamol, 500 mg, when my hip's playing up. I don't like taking tablets for the sake of it.
That's the right way round. I notice you've got osteoporosis on your notes, and the high blood pressure.
That's me. Osteoporosis, they said, which is why the hip went when I only tripped on the cat.
That cat's a menace, Doctor. ~
He is, but we'll keep him. Right, let's do your numbers. ~
Oh, I do love a numbers day. ~
Pulse 72, blood pressure 134 over 80, temperature 36.5, oxygen 97 percent, and you weigh 58 kilos.
Is that good or do I need feeding up? ~
It's steady, and it's the same as last time, so you're not losing weight. Since you've had the fracture, I'd like to arrange a bone density scan, to see how strong the bones are now.
Is that the one where you lie flat on a bed? ~
That's it. Painless and quick. You don't need to do anything special for it. ~
Will it tell me why I've got to take that Sunday tablet? ~
It'll tell us whether the treatment is doing its job, and whether we need to change it. ~
Right. Good. I like to know why I'm doing things. ~
And I'd like to see you again in three months, once the scan is done, to talk about the results.
I'll book that, Doris. I'll put it in the diary by the fridge. ~
Doctor, can I ask you something? About bingo. ~
Go on. ~
Is it all right to go back on a Thursday if Bev drives me? ~
As long as you use the frame and don't rush, I don't see why not. ~
Marvellous. Thank you, love. ~
